title: How many steps from 5 to 9 along the number line?
description: A walker goes from five to nine along the number line and the steps are counted between the numbers. The count is written as an addition and as a take away. Keeko's doubt is that the count of numbers is the count of steps.
teaching_notes: One idea: the movement from five to nine is the number of steps between them, four, and it matches nine take away five. Watch for students who count the numbers five, six, seven, eight and nine and say five steps.

source: If, from 5 you wish to go over to 9, how far must you travel
video_script.why: The child sees that the movement from one number to another on the number line is the count of steps between them, and that it matches target minus start.
video_script.substitution: The book's own number line, walking forward from five to nine.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book, with a walker going forward from five to nine
video_script.wrong_move: counts the numbers five, six, seven, eight and nine instead of the steps between them
video_script.payoff_line: The journey from five to nine is four steps forward.
maths_rules: stand on 5, walk right: 6, 7, 8, 9 is 4 steps
slip: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 are five numbers, but the first number is where the walker already stands, so there are 4 steps
video_script.design: A number line from 0 to 10 with a walker on 5; the steps are counted one at a time while the walker moves right.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 10 with a walker standing on 5 and 9 lit up

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the number line is drawn
marks.ask: the number 9 lights up and a question mark appears between them

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the number line.
<bookmark mark='walker'/>You stand on five and wish to go over to nine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far must you travel along the line?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: right = forward, left = backward; one step = the gap between neighbouring numbers

marks.dir: an arrow to the right is marked forward and an arrow to the left is marked backward
marks.gap: the gap between 5 and 6 is bracketed as one step

narration: <bookmark mark='dir'/>On the number line, to the right is forward, and to the left is backward.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>One step is the gap between two neighbouring numbers.

marks.given: the start and the target are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the starting number is five, and the target number is nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: how far to travel

marks.find: the words how far are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how far to travel.

beats.on_screen: walker steps 5 to 6 to 7 to 8 to 9; step count 1, 2, 3, 4

marks.walk: the walker steps from 5 to 6, 7, 8 and 9 while the count 1, 2, 3, 4 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='walk'/>Step one, walk forward from five, and count the steps, not the numbers.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Six is one step, seven is two, eight is three, and nine is four.

marks.rule: the line Starting number + Movement = Target number is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, starting number plus movement is the target number.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Five plus four is nine.

marks.rule: the line Target number - Starting number = Movement is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, the same fact as a take away, target number take away starting number is the movement.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Nine take away five is four.

marks.ans: 4 steps forward is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The walker has made four steps in the forward direction.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The journey from five to nine is four steps forward.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 counted as five numbers; the first number 5 is crossed out because the walker already stands there

marks.doubt: the numbers 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 are counted one to five
marks.fix: the count on 5 is struck out and the walker is shown standing there
marks.why: four gaps are left, bracketed between 5 and 9

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it is five steps, because five, six, seven, eight and nine are five numbers.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the walker already stands on five, so that number needs no step.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Only the gaps are steps, and there are four of them.
